reason: Almost all weighty bills change procedural protections of suspects and defendants in arrest, search, questioning, evidence and trial. On the 'toward' side, enforcement powers expand: organized-crime and illegal-weapons laws (1, 2, 12, 14, 24), detention until end of proceedings and stricter bail (13, 16, 23, 28), no state-funded defense for security offenders (6), and privileged therapy records (9). On the 'away' side, protections grow: exclusion of illegally obtained evidence (3, 27), limits on state appeals against acquittals (4, 15), adapted arrest and questioning for people with disabilities (7, 10, 17, 34), a lawyer present when minors are questioned (19, 25, 26), time limits on investigations (18, 21), strip-search rules (11) and a Basic Law on rights in criminal proceedings (31). The statement asks exactly this trade-off, names a price ('even if the risk of convicting innocent people grows') and keeps one idea. Bill 8 (administrative detention) and bill 22 (psychiatric opinion deadline) are light or borderline and do not change the verdict.
